question: would approximate string matching recover quotes and participant names that the exact rules miss, and at what risk

definitions.quote_population: opinions of people with at least one matched turn, with at least one quote extracted by udv_pipeline.extract_quotes, whose exact match (find_opinion_turn_quote_match) has no trusted prefix of 6+ words
definitions.eligible_quote: an extracted quote with 6+ whitespace words
definitions.gain: a population opinion whose fuzzy score reaches the threshold at the first prefix level, in configured order, that reaches it; the sentence is the one enclosing the aligned span in that turn
definitions.agrees_with_encoder: sentences_agree between the fuzzy sentence and the reference run's top-1 sentence, only for records whose reference tier is semantic; it is a weak precision proxy, because the encoder embeds the full opinion, quote included, so both signals see the quote text and are not independent
definitions.null: quotes that should not occur in the person's speech, aligned against the same person's turns with the same scorer; the rate of draws at or above the threshold estimates how often a threshold is reached by chance; same_hearing_other_person is topic-matched and may include genuine repetitions
definitions.expected_chance_matches: null rate times the population opinions with an eligible quote
definitions.positive_control: opinions with a trusted exact prefix, the exact prefix aligned with the same scorer; score 100 and agreement with the exact sentence are expected
definitions.encoder_baseline: on the positive control, how often the production encoder's top-1 sentence, recomputed from the cached embeddings of the production run (no encoding here), agrees with the sentence of the trusted exact quote; it is the agreement rate the proxy reaches on quote sentences known by exact matching, so an agreement rate among fuzzy gains is read against it, not against 1
definitions.elsewhere: the same prefixes aligned against every turn of the hearing not matched to the person, at the accepted level; a gain whose quote scores higher elsewhere may belong to another speaker (misattribution, a quote read aloud, or the person quoting someone)
definitions.encoder_cache_consistency: for population opinions, whether the cached top-1 equals the reference run's evidence; with the production run as reference every compared pair must match
definitions.bands: opinions accepted at a threshold and not at the next one, with the sentence of the lower threshold
definitions.names_population: participants with no matched turn under resolve_person_speech
definitions.names_status: unique: best at or above the threshold and the best disjoint rival below it; ambiguous: a disjoint rival also at or above it; already_assigned: the best speaker shares turns with a participant the exact rules resolved; metrics_disagree (rule both): the two metrics pick different speakers; contested: two unresolved participants of one hearing would take the same turns
definitions.impostor_control: participants the exact rules resolved, scored against the hearing's speakers that share no turn with their own; the rate at or above the threshold estimates how often a name reaches it on a different speaker
definitions.quote_support: opinions of the participant whose quote has an exact prefix match (find_opinion_turn_quote_match) inside the candidate speaker's turns
definitions.bootstrap: 1000 resamples of whole hearings, 95% percentile interval, fixed seed

review.blinding_rule: the review sheets <run>_quotes_review.jsonl and <run>_names_review.jsonl show only what a judgment needs. Quotes: hearing_id, participant, role, opinion, its extracted quotes, the turn header and the candidate passage with context_chars of context on each side inside the turn; one row per distinct candidate passage of an opinion, every method and prefix level that proposed it merged into that row. Names: hearing_id, participant, role and opinions, and the candidate speaker's header name, party information, turn count and first speech excerpt; one row per distinct candidate speaker of a participant. Rows are in a seeded random order and item ids follow that order. Method, prefix level, prefix, score, encoder agreement, encoder tier and support type, exact short-quote match, scores in other speakers' turns, split, metric ranks and scores, assignment to a resolved participant and quote support are written only to the matching <run>_*_review_key.json. The reviewer opens only the two sheets and the transcripts, never the keys, <run>_quotes.jsonl, <run>_names.jsonl or the report files
known_leaks: rows that share an opinion (or a participant) are separate rows, so the reviewer can count how many distinct candidates were proposed for it; an opinion with a single row had every method and prefix level at the same passage

every quote row has at least one proposal scoring quotes.review_min_score or more, and every name row belongs to a participant whose best candidate scores names.review_min_score or more under some metric, so the sheets hold only proposals above those floors
hearing_id is shown so the transcript can be opened; the split is not shown, but it follows from hearing_id through the split manifest

splits.test_policy: test is never read unless --final-test is passed; nothing in this experiment is fitted or chosen, thresholds are only swept and reported

reference.selection_rule: first run in the list whose <run>.jsonl and <run>_coverage.json both exist; the evidence of its semantic records is the production encoder's top-1 sentence

encoder_baseline.rule: the production run writes per-hearing embeddings keyed by encoder name, revision and device label; this experiment only reads those files (cosine argmax per opinion over the person's sentences, first index on ties, as in build_udvs) and never encodes, so it runs on CPU; a hearing without cached files is counted and left out of the baseline

quotes.prefix_rule: same prefixes as the exact pipeline: the first min(level, len(words)) whitespace words of each extracted quote, kept only with min_prefix_words or more; levels are tried in order, as in the exact cascade
quotes.text_folding: per character: accents stripped and lowercased, a character whose folded form is not one character keeps its lowercase or original form, so offsets in the folded text are offsets in the whitespace-normalized turn text
quotes.char_scorer: rapidfuzz.fuzz.partial_ratio_alignment(folded prefix, folded turn text); when the turn is shorter than the prefix, rapidfuzz.fuzz.ratio over the whole turn
quotes.token_scorer: rapidfuzz.fuzz.partial_ratio_alignment over lists of \w+ tokens of the folded texts; for a window of the same length this equals 100 * in-order matched words / prefix tokens; when the turn has fewer tokens than the prefix, rapidfuzz.fuzz.ratio over the whole turn
quotes.search_unit: each matched turn of the person separately
quotes.null_rule: each draw takes as many eligible quotes as the opinion has, from the pool, without replacement, and aligns them against the same person's turns; same_hearing_other_person draws quotes of other participants of the same hearing (topic-matched, may contain real repetitions), other_hearing_same_split draws quotes of other hearings of the same split

names.name_normalization: udv_pipeline.normalize_name (accents stripped, uppercase), then only \w+ tokens joined by one space
names.speaker_definition: each distinct normalized turn name candidate (udv_pipeline.turn_name_candidates) of the hearing, with the set of turns that carry it
names.second_best_rule: highest-scoring speaker whose turn set is disjoint from the best speaker's, so aliases of the same turns are not rivals

review.filled_sheet_rule: a review sheet with a judgment on any row is never overwritten: rerunning the experiment stops before writing anything

label_definitions.match: one of the opinion's quotations starts in the candidate passage: its first words are there, allowing differences of spelling, accents, punctuation or a few words
label_definitions.no_match: no quotation of the opinion starts in the candidate passage
label_definitions.unsure: the passage and its context do not allow a decision

label_definitions.same_person: the candidate speaker is the participant (the name, role, party information and speech fit, allowing spelling variants of the name)
label_definitions.different_person: the candidate speaker is someone else
label_definitions.unsure: the sheet does not allow a decision

precision.precision_rule: utils.fuzzy_review_precision joins each filled sheet with its key and the rows file the key was built from (sha256 checked). Quotes: for each method and threshold, the gains of that threshold (first prefix level reaching it, as in the gains section) inherit the judgment of the row that shows their candidate passage; bands take the gains of a threshold that the next threshold does not keep. Names: for each rule and threshold, the participants that rule would resolve (status unique and not contested) inherit the judgment of the row of their best speaker. precision = positive / (positive + negative), unsure left out; precision_unsure_as_error counts unsure as errors; intervals resample the hearings that contribute accepted items, whole; the Wilson interval ignores the hearing clustering and is given for reference only. The report is computed only when every row of both sheets has a valid judgment, so no precision number is seen during the review
